clue.text: Provide speech in praise of political party?

parts.note: CON is the short form of Conservative, the British political party
a tribute is an address honouring someone

explanation.surface: A question about giving a eulogy to celebrate a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads the parts in reverse: the praise speech is 'of' the party, but in the answer the party comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To give money or effort to a cause is to supply it, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: One who makes dresses more comfortable round the stomach

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: cosier means snugger, more comfortable
tum is a familiar word for the stomach

explanation.surface: A dressmaker lets out garments to make them less tight at the waist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' signals the container; 'dresses' suggests frocks, but this maker supplies theatrical outfits.
explanation.definitionFit: A costumier makes or supplies costumes, the clothes actors wear, which is dressing them.

clue.text: Mad chumps

explanation.surface: Insane fools.
explanation.definitionFit: Crazy people are said to be bonkers; chumps here are heads, which slang also calls these.

clue.text: Split up again, see, after dire trouble

indicators.note: the word for see is placed after the stirred-up letters
to trouble something is to disturb it, so its letters are stirred up

parts.note: vide is Latin for see, used in references

explanation.surface: An instruction to divide things once more, following a dreadful problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' makes REDI from the anagram; 'after' sets the Latin footnote word for 'see' behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: To divide something a second time is to separate it into parts once more.

clue.text: Insect, tiresome sort, right?

parts.note: a bore is a dull, tedious person

explanation.surface: A question whether an irritating bug is a dull type.
explanation.definitionFit: A borer is a beetle or larva that tunnels into wood or plants.

clue.text: Short-term employee getting uppity about a painting technique

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker

indicators.note: in a down clue going up reverses the letters

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A temporary worker becomes arrogant over a method of painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting uppity' in a down clue turns RE (about) upward into ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera is painting with pigment bound in egg yolk, an old artistic method.

clue.text: Member of wedding party travels with mother? That's in order

indicators.note: the pieces are placed within the word for order

parts.note: to bid someone is to order them
rides means travels on a horse or vehicle
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A wedding guest goes along with her mother, as is proper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container; 'That's in order' reads as 'that is proper', but 'order' supplies the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridesmaid is a woman or girl who attends the bride at a wedding.

clue.text: A goddess featured in sacred texts

parts.note: Vesta is the Roman goddess of the hearth

explanation.surface: A goddess appears in holy writings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Avesta is the collection of Zoroastrian scriptures, a religious canon.

clue.text: Cleric, one in position to be called on again

parts.note: REV is short for Reverend, a title for a member of the clergy
the Roman numeral for one is I
something sited is placed or located in position

explanation.surface: A clergyman takes up a post where he will be visited a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: To visit is to call on someone, so calling on them a second time is a repeat visit.

clue.text: Capital returns from remortgaging

indicators.note: the letters found are read backwards, as if coming back the way they went
the letters are taken out of the single word that follows

explanation.surface: Money comes back to someone who has taken out a new mortgage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' picks EMOR out of 'remortgaging', and 'returns' turns that run backwards; 'Capital' looks financial but means a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian capital city, seat of the national government.

clue.text: Serve his pud well-cooked

indicators.note: food that is well cooked has been thoroughly worked over, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An instruction to bring out a man's pudding after cooking it thoroughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well-cooked' rearranges the letters of HIS PUD.
explanation.definitionFit: To dish up a meal is to put it out on plates for diners, a phrasal synonym of serve.

clue.text: By the sound of it, works as supervisor abroad

indicators.note: these words tell us the answer is a word that is pronounced like another phrase in the clue

parts.note: one who works as a supervisor oversees staff

explanation.surface: Someone is apparently employed as a manager in a foreign country.
explanation.definitionFit: Being across the sea means being in a foreign country.

clue.text: MI6 boss secures shelter: he's in need of rest

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so one piece holds another inside

parts.note: MI6 is the British secret intelligence service, a world of spies
lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
a head is a chief or boss

explanation.surface: The head of British intelligence finds a safe house, needing a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secures' signals the container; MI6 is Britain's foreign intelligence agency, so its chief is a spymaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleepyhead is a drowsy person who wants to go to bed, so needing rest.

clue.text: Most of the plant is inactive

indicators.note: all but the final letter of the plant's name is used

parts.note: statice is sea lavender, a flowering plant often dried

explanation.surface: Much of a factory or a garden plant is doing nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' removes the last letter from STATICE, the sea lavender plant; 'plant' could suggest a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Something static is motionless and still, which is an idle or unmoving state.

clue.text: Recommend a legal expert

explanation.surface: An instruction to suggest a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to speak in favour of something; as a noun it is a barrister or lawyer who pleads cases in court.

clue.text: The chef has a hand in it

definitions.text: The chef has a hand in it

parts.words: The chef has a hand in it
parts.note: 'has a hand in' usually means is involved, but here the cook literally puts a hand inside a padded kitchen item

explanation.surface: The cook is involved in something.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded mitt protects a cook's hand when taking hot dishes from the oven.

clue.text: Coin forged in US, dear

indicators.note: forged means faked or hammered into a new shape, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone's counterfeit coin is made in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forged' rearranges IN US DEAR; a denarius was a silver coin of ancient Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The denarius was the standard silver piece of Roman money.

clue.text: Tale-teller cunningly ensnared

indicators.note: doing something cunningly involves craft and twisting, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A storyteller has been trapped by trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cunningly' rearranges ENSNARED; Hans Christian Andersen wrote fairy tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Christian Andersen was the Danish writer famous for fairy stories such as The Little Mermaid.

clue.text: Refuse product on sale around Christmas?

parts.note: Dec, short for December, is the month around Christmas
a line is a type of goods a shop stocks

explanation.surface: A question whether a shopper turns down goods offered in the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' could be the noun for rubbish, but it is the verb meaning turn down.
explanation.definitionFit: To decline an offer is to turn it down.

clue.text: Bird and animal kept confined

parts.note: a pen is a female swan
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A bird and a beast are shut up together in an enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: PEN is the female swan and TUP a ram, words more familiar to crossword solvers than to most people.
explanation.definitionFit: Feelings or creatures held back with no release are restrained, kept in.

clue.text: British in experiment concerning an ethnic group?

indicators.note: the letter goes within the word for experiment

parts.note: a trial is a test or experiment

explanation.surface: A question whether a British test is about a particular people.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribal relates to a tribe, a social group sharing descent and culture.

clue.text: TV programme featuring medic and American retiree

parts.note: doc is a familiar word for a doctor
US stands for United States, so American
OAP is old-age pensioner, the British term for someone retired

explanation.surface: A television show stars a doctor and an elderly American pensioner.
explanation.walkthrough: OAP (old-age pensioner) is the British abbreviation for a retired person.
explanation.definitionFit: A docusoap is a fly-on-the-wall documentary series that follows real people like a soap opera.

clue.text: Demonstrated how to come between partners at the table

indicators.note: one piece is placed between the two letters of the other

parts.note: in bridge, South and North are partners at the card table, abbreviated S and N

explanation.surface: Someone was taught how to interfere between a couple at a dinner table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come between' puts HOW between S and N, the South and North bridge partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shown has been displayed or made clear to someone.

clue.text: Like a fit of shivering when one is stuck in a stream

indicators.note: one piece is lodged inside the other, as something stuck in a channel

parts.note: a gush is a sudden stream of liquid
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone shivers as they are trapped in a cold stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is stuck in' puts I inside GUSH, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: An ague is a feverish fit with chills, so this adjective describes such shaking.

clue.text: Eats hot dish of meat and vegetables

parts.note: to have food is to eat it, so has means eats
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone eats a warm stew of meat and veg.
explanation.definitionFit: Hash is chopped meat fried with potatoes and other vegetables.

clue.text: Drinker in Mayfair district? Not so

parts.note: Mayfair, a wealthy area of London, is in the W1 postal district, read as letters WI
no is a denial that something is so

explanation.surface: A question whether a heavy drinker would be found in the smart London district of Mayfair.
explanation.walkthrough: W1 is the London postcode for Mayfair, a wealthy West End district; the 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A wino is a habitual drinker of cheap alcohol, often homeless.

clue.text: In the morning, speak briefly with a lover

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, indicates morning

indicators.note: a shortened word, here the last letter dropped

parts.note: to orate is to make a speech

explanation.surface: Early in the day, someone has a quick word with their partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts the last letter from ORATE, leaving ORAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a woman who is loved, a sweetheart or girlfriend.

clue.text: What's afoot at Wimbledon?

parts.note: 'afoot' usually means happening, but here means literally on the foot, and Wimbledon is the London grass-court championship, so this asks for players' footwear

explanation.surface: A question about what is going on at the famous tennis championships.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the annual tennis championship held in south-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Players wear rubber-soled sports footwear on the courts.
